name: Hoi An food guide
summary: Hoi An’s bowl is cao lầu, tossed while it is hot. White rose dumplings are a small warm plate. Bánh đập is the Cẩm Nam cracker. Nước mót is the herb drink, and the herb list depends on who printed it.
body: Eat cao lầu in the old town. People here call these noodles bánh. The heritage centre’s 11 August 2025 article separates them from mì. The noodles are thick, the broth only wets them, and the herbs are from Trà Quế. The bowl looks related to mì Quảng. It is a different dish.

White rose dumplings are eaten warm, one at a bite. Vietnam Tourism says the wrapper is rice flour. The conservation centre’s 4 September 2024 article, republishing Dân Việt, says wheat flour. Chicken rice is shredded chicken and yellow rice. Vietnam Tourism pairs it with herbs, chicken soup, and a sour papaya salad. The conservation centre’s 4 December 2025 article prints rau răm and ginger fish sauce. Its 30 October 2024 note prints pickled vegetables and chili sauce.

Bánh mì is the morning stall in the old town. Bánh đập, in Cẩm Nam, is the cracker you break by hand and often eat with hến xào. Hoành thánh is the wonton, in broth or fried. Bánh xoài, near the Japanese bridge, is a chewy sweet named for its shape. Vietnam Tourism fills it with peanuts and brown sugar. The 4 December 2025 article fills it with peanut, sesame, and ginger. Nước mót is the herb drink. Vietnam Tourism lists ginger, lemongrass, cinnamon, licorice, lemon, green tea, chamomile, and monk fruit. The December article lists monk fruit, licorice, chrysanthemum, and lotus leaf.
specialtiesLead: The dishes to know by name. A stall clock that was not printed is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: More Hoi An dishes
paragraphs: These are the other specialties the conservation centre, Vietnam Tourism, and Danang Fantasticity name. Bánh ú tro and bánh ít are named as market gifts on the 7 June 2023 market article and are not described.

spots.name: Banh uot thit nuong
spots.note: Roll grilled meat in wet rice paper. Vietnam Tourism says pork on lemongrass skewers, with salad, herbs, cucumber, star fruit, and a dip of soybean paste, peanuts, sesame, fish sauce, and chili. The 4 December 2025 article says grilled beef and a rich, mildly hot peanut-butter sauce. Danang Fantasticity does not name the animal. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bun thit nuong
spots.note: Barbecued pork, rice noodles, and salad greens in a thicker sauce than northern bún chả, on Vietnam Tourism’s Hoi An food article. The 4 December 2025 article adds pork skewers, herbs, crisp chả ram, and sweet-sour fish sauce. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh dap
spots.note: Press a crisp rice-paper sheet onto a soft steamed sheet. The 30 May 2023 article dips it in Cửa Đại anchovy mắm cái with sugar and fried-shallot oil. Danang Fantasticity’s Hội An section uses anchovy mắm nêm with sugar, pineapple or lime, and red chili. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Hen xao
spots.note: Stir-fried clam with onion, scallion, and chili, finished with crushed peanuts, eaten with the cracker. The 30 October 2024 note puts the snack in Cẩm Nam. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Hoanh thanh
spots.note: Fried, in a clear pork-bone broth, or on thin wheat noodles. The 28 June 2011 article fills the dumpling with land shrimp. The 4 September 2024 article fills it with shrimp and pork. A street and the hour are Check on arrival.

spots.name: Grilled pork rice-paper rolls
spots.note: The 7 June 2023 list rolls grilled pork with herbs, star fruit or sour pineapple, green banana, a little bún, and fish sauce or mắm nêm. It is not the boiled Da Nang lunch. A street and the hour are Check on arrival.

spots.name: Tam huu
spots.note: One cooked land shrimp, a slice of boiled pork, and mint, tied with a blanched scallion and dipped in sweet-sour fish sauce. Danang Fantasticity’s 16 April 2024 essay places it in the vegetable village. A house and the hour are Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bun mam nem
spots.note: Soft rice noodles with a rich fermented sauce of garlic, chili, and shrimp, on the 4 September 2024 article. A street and the hour are Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh canh
spots.note: Thick noodles in rice flour or bột lọc, with roasted pork, fish cake, herbs, or seafood, plus green chili and garlic-chili fish sauce. This is not the Da Nang snakehead bowl. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Chao ngheu
spots.note: Morning clam porridge with ginger, scallion, and rau răm. The 4 September 2024 article does not name a street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Chao gao luc
spots.note: Evening brown-rice porridge with braised fish, chili, and green winter melon. A street and the hour are Check on arrival.

spots.name: Be thui
spots.note: Danang Fantasticity places bê thui Cầu Mống in Điện Bàn. The 7 June 2023 market article rolls grilled veal, herbs, and anchovy mắm in rice paper and does not say that plate is Cầu Mống. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Chan ga cay
spots.note: A chicken-foot snack in chili, garlic, and onion. The 4 September 2024 article does not name the rest of the sauce, or a street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Oc xao bo toi
spots.note: Snails stir-fried with butter and garlic, eaten with bánh mì, on the 7 June 2023 list. Evening. A street and the hour are Check on arrival.

spots.name: Oc hap sa gung
spots.note: Snails steamed with lemongrass and ginger, named as an evening plate on the 7 June 2023 list. A further recipe was not printed. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Oc xao me
spots.note: Snails stir-fried with tamarind, named as an evening plate on the 7 June 2023 list. A further recipe was not printed. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh xoai
spots.note: A chewy sweet named for its shape. Vietnam Tourism uses peanuts and brown sugar. The 4 December 2025 article uses peanut, sesame, and ginger. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Nuoc mot
spots.note: A herb drink, cold or hot, usually taken away. Vietnam Tourism and the 4 December 2025 article print different herbs. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Che bap
spots.note: Corn sweet soup with rock sugar and coconut milk. Danang Fantasticity says the dish did not start in Hội An and that the corn is from Cẩm Nam. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Che dau xanh
spots.note: Mung-bean sweet soup, fragrant with coconut milk, on the 4 December 2025 article. A stall and the hour are Check on arrival.

spots.name: Che hat sen
spots.note: Lotus-seed sweet soup, fragrant with coconut milk, on the 4 December 2025 article. A stall and the hour are Check on arrival.

spots.name: Xi ma
spots.note: Black-sesame sweet soup, also called chè mè đen. Danang Fantasticity says it is sweet, rich, and cool, and names Cụ Thiều’s shoulder pole without a street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh dau xanh
spots.note: A gift cake with a pork and mung-bean filling, or a meatless cake, eaten with hot tea. Danang Fantasticity’s 16 April 2024 essay names no street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Mam ca com
spots.note: Anchovy sauce from Cửa Đại and Cù Lao Chàm. Spoon it on hot rice, or dip boiled greens. The 7 June 2023 market article also names other sauces and does not describe them. The hour is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Regional dishes
paragraphs: Mì Quảng is the Quảng Nam bowl, eaten in town when the ride to Da Nang is another day. Vietnam Tourism says the noodles are flat and turmeric-yellow, with a ladle of broth, herbs, peanuts, and a cracker. The 4 December 2025 article keeps the broth shallow and adds Trà Quế herbs. Toss it. It is not cao lầu.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: The old town is the meal. Chợ Hội An has a food hall the heritage note names for cao lầu, and the 7 June 2023 market article sends you there for mắm cá cơm. The street number and the hours are Check on arrival. UNESCO’s list text includes an open market inside the property and does not name the street.
The night market sits on Nguyễn Hoàng, Công nữ Ngọc Hoa, Trần Quý Cáp, and Bạch Đằng, close to the old-town centre. The 2023 note does not print an open or a close. Check on arrival.

Tân Thành, in the fishing village now inside Hoi An Tây, holds a weekend market the ministry article says is usually on Saturday and Sunday. A later week can move. Check on arrival. Cẩm Nam is the bánh đập lane. Thái Phiên, early, is the street the 4 December 2025 article names for noodles and rolls. Stalls along the Hoài sell bánh ướt. None of those clocks is printed.

spots.name: Hoi An market
spots.note: The food hall for cao lầu, and the counters for mắm cá cơm. A street number and the hours are Check on arrival.

spots.name: Hoi An night market
spots.address: Nguyễn Hoàng, Công nữ Ngọc Hoa, Trần Quý Cáp, and Bạch Đằng
spots.note: Evening stalls close to the old-town centre. The 7 June 2023 note does not print an open or a close. Check on arrival.

spots.name: Tan Thanh weekend market
spots.note: A fishing-village market the June 2024 ministry article says is usually on Saturday and Sunday. A later week can move. Check on arrival.

spots.name: Cam Nam
spots.note: The lane for bánh đập and hến xào. The 30 May 2023 article and the 30 October 2024 note place the cracker here. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Thai Phien
spots.note: Early morning noodles and rolls, on the 4 December 2025 article. A clock was not printed. Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Bánh mì is the baguette from a street stall in the old town, the morning it is baked. Point at the fillings if there is a choice. Danang Fantasticity describes the Hội An loaf as dense, with a crisp crust, still hot, and a slightly sweet crumb. Cháo nghêu is the other morning bowl: clams, ginger, scallion, and rau răm. Thái Phiên is the early street for noodles and rolls. The clocks are Check on arrival.

seoTitle: Hoi An food guide — cao lầu, dumplings, and bánh đập
seoDescription: Toss cao lầu while it is hot. White rose is one warm bite. Bánh đập is the Cẩm Nam cracker, and nước mót is the herb drink. Stall hours are Check on arrival.
